import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Create a DataFrame with duplicates across multiple columns
data = {
    'first_name': ['John', 'john', 'JOHN', 'Jane', 'jane'],
    'last_name': ['Smith', 'smith', 'SMITH', 'Doe', 'DOE'],
    'email': ['john@email.com', 'JOHN@EMAIL.COM', 'john@email.com', 'jane@email.com', 'JANE@EMAIL.COM'],
    'score': [85, 85, 90, 92, 92]
}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Normalize text columns for comparison
df['first_name_norm'] = df['first_name'].str.lower().str.strip()
df['last_name_norm'] = df['last_name'].str.lower().str.strip()
df['email_norm'] = df['email'].str.lower().str.strip()

# Drop duplicates based on normalized columns, keeping highest score
df_sorted = df.sort_values('score', ascending=False)
df_clean = df_sorted.drop_duplicates(subset=['email_norm'], keep='first')

# Clean up temporary columns
df_clean = df_clean.drop(columns=['first_name_norm', 'last_name_norm', 'email_norm'])

print(f"Original: {len(df)} rows, Clean: {len(df_clean)} rows")
print(df_clean)
